title: HNB in Croatia’s inflation debate
subtitle: Media evidence for monetary communication
paper_title: Pasivno zamijenjena: cijena inflacije koju ne mjeri indeks potrošačkih cijena
paper_subtitle: Od inflacijskog vala do dezinflacije: institucionalni jaz u pažnji HNB-a 2021.–2026.
sample: January 2021–May 2026, with a break in usable text coverage
dataset_last_observed_day_status: Documented in the dataset README; later periods are not the headline analytical sample.
citation: Palić, P., & Sikić, L. (2026). Pasivno zamijenjena: cijena inflacije koju ne mjeri indeks potrošačkih cijena. Extended research draft, 17 September 2026. Hrvatsko katoličko sveučilište.
contributions: Both researchers are named as authors in the manuscript. Individual contribution roles are not specified.
question: How visible is the central bank when inflation dominates the news?
answer: Higher inflation accompanies lower relative institutional visibility in the primary models. Within April 2024–May 2026, visibility also declines after accounting for inflation. These findings identify questions for closer communication analysis; they do not measure public understanding or the effect of HNB policy.

findings.headline: Higher inflation accompanies lower visibility
findings.text: In the primary weekly model, a one percentage point increase in HICP inflation is associated with a wider attention gap, after accounting for the model’s controls.
findings.caveat: This is an association. Statistical significance does not survive every time-control specification.
findings.implication: A question for HNB: does institutional coverage keep pace with the wider inflation debate?

findings.headline: Visibility declines within the later period
findings.text: From April 2024 to May 2026, the gap rises within the newer data source after controlling for inflation and other regressors. A positive trend also appears when the analysis keeps only common sources.
findings.caveat: Changing coverage within sources remains possible. This does not establish hysteresis or a causal effect of disinflation.
findings.implication: A next step: investigate changing coverage, institutional attribution and the uptake of specific explanations.

findings.headline: A stable link to expectations is not established
findings.text: Forward projections of consumer expectations depend on how monthly survey information is assigned to weeks and which controls are used. They do not robustly establish a persistent predictive channel.
findings.caveat: Some horizons are significant under other specifications. The survey balance does not measure long-term anchoring or trust.
findings.implication: A research priority: measure audience exposure and understanding separately from media representation.
